items.title: Stand up re-verification CI for the first adopted record surface (scheduled re-fetch + check + drift alarm)
items.note: Follows A-1 — the reconciliation picks the first surface to adopt (likely Tao's optimization-constants inventory or a subset of erdosproblems.com bounds). CI: scheduled job re-fetches sources, re-runs checks, diffs against the ledger, opens a finding on drift. Public status page comes after the pattern holds, and the public flip is adversarial-review + David-gated. Surface selected 2026-07-22: teorth/optimizationproblems (~85 constants, structure documented in reconciliation #1). CI checks: re-fetch constant files, diff tables vs ledger copy, cross-check external surfaces (erdosproblems.com, Wikipedia, paper abstracts), finding on drift. STOOD UP 2026-07-23: scripts/reverify.mjs (--snapshot/--check) + .github/workflows/reverify.yml (daily cron 09:17 UTC + push + manual; drift -> failed run + auto-filed GitHub issue). Snapshot: 109 files @ a002311. Synthetic-drift demo PASS (scripts/reverify.test.mjs, runs in CI every time, no network). Cross-surface half shipped same day: scripts/check-claims.mjs + ledger/claims.json (7 claims; 6 fetchable HOLD across Tao-at-HEAD + arXiv abs + ar5iv + Wikipedia, C-7 erdosproblems reports UNVERIFIED by design since the site 403s bots). Both checks + both selftests wired into reverify.yml; a failure files one combined finding issue. Remaining for close: green on schedule (30-day streak per G-1). 2026-07-24 — ALARM WAS NOT ACTUALLY ARMED: both live checks piped into `tee` and the GitHub Actions default shell is `bash -e {0}` with no pipefail, so a drift exit-1 was reported as exit 0, the job passed, and `if: failure()` never filed the issue. The synthetic-drift self-test could not catch it (it tested the script's exit code, not the workflow's consumption of it). Fixed with `shell: bash` on both piped steps; reverify.test.mjs now asserts every piped workflow step declares it (negative control performed). Finding: docs/findings/2026-07-24-drift-alarm-was-never-armed.md.
items.closeWhen: CI green on a schedule for one adopted surface with drift detection demonstrated on a synthetic change.
items.note2: PIN EXTENSION SHIPPED 2026-07-24 eve (David unheld the 7/23 feature hold in-pane: 'Accidental hold. Please proceed.'): scripts/extract-pins.mjs generates 216 claim pins covering all 109 constants (1b.md stays hand-pinned as C-1/C-3) — ledger/claims.json now 7 hand + 216 generated = 223 claims, 222/222 fetchable HOLD live, C-7 UNVERIFIED by design. DESIGN DECISION: pins assert the LAST-LISTED row of each bounds table (verbatim raw line), NOT 'the record' — numeric record-ranking is defeated by symbolic cells ($K_{DR}+10^{-26}$), negatives, O(.) asymptotics (verified against the corpus; a min/max prototype mis-picked 10a/21a/41a), and auto-asserting 'record' 216x would put unverified statements in our own ledger. Last-listed is true by construction; an appended new record trips the mirror diff instead. NEW DISCIPLINE: after any deliberate --snapshot, re-run extract-pins.mjs and commit the regenerated pins — pins are the post-snapshot ratchet (a moved row stays BROKEN until deliberately re-pinned). check-claims.mjs now per-URL fetch-caches and counts (not lists) held claims so a real BREAK can't drown below the fold. Commit 22fa79c.

items.title: Alarm files NO finding issue when the job fails before the drift/claims steps run (self-test failure path)
items.note: Found by the 2026-07-25 gate-execution sweep by EXECUTING reverify.yml's `Open finding` body under GitHub's exact shell semantics (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`), not by reading it. When either self-test step fails, `finding.txt` is never created; the step's `cat finding.txt` then exits 1 under `-eo pipefail`, so the step dies BEFORE `gh issue create` and no finding issue is filed. Two consequences: (1) an instrument failure produces a red job but no issue — the drift alarm is silent about its own breakage, which is the same family as the 2026-07-24 never-armed defect; (2) the only diagnostic emitted is `cat: finding.txt: No such file or directory`, which points at the wrong thing. NOT a drift-masking bug: the job still goes red and the workflow-failure notification still fires, so a real drift is never hidden. Severity LOW. Evidence: with finding.txt absent the step exits 1; with a real synthetic drift present it produces title `Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)`, and with a real BROKEN claim it produces `Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)` — both branches of the title extractor verified FIRING against real tool output.
items.closeWhen: The Open-finding step either files a legibly-titled instrument-failure issue when finding.txt is absent, or a deliberate decision is recorded that a red job alone is sufficient for self-test failures.
items.resolution: FIXED 2026-07-25, same day, David-decided. He chose 'file an instrument-failure issue' over 'a red job is enough' — rationale: a red CI run on a once-a-day lane is easy to scroll past, and the failure mode being hidden is our own instrument going quiet, which is precisely what this lane claims to catch. The Open-finding step now branches on `[ -s finding.txt ]`: with check output it behaves exactly as before ('Drift: <what moved>'); without it, it files 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (<date>)' with an explicit '(no check output — the job failed before the drift/claims steps ran)' body instead of dying at `cat` and filing nothing. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not inspection: the step body was extracted verbatim from the deployed YAML, the `gh issue create` call stripped, and run under GitHub's exact shell (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`) against all three real inputs — absent finding.txt => 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (2026-07-25)'; real injected mirror drift => 'Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)'; real broken pin => 'Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)'. No regression on the two paths that already worked; pipefail guard still passes (step keeps `shell: bash`).
items.note2: SUPERSEDED — read `resolution` above; this fix SHIPPED 2026-07-25 and is live in .github/workflows/reverify.yml (the `[ -s finding.txt ]` branch + the `Instrument failure:` title). Kept only as the pre-fix reasoning. ORIGINAL: READY FIX (deliberately NOT shipped in the sweep — it changes WHEN the alarm files, and the alarm surface is this lane's most load-bearing artifact; 7/24's lesson is that changes here get deliberated): guard the cat and make the title honest, e.g. `cat finding.txt 2>/dev/null || echo '(no check output — job failed before the drift/claims steps ran; see the failed step above)'` plus a title fallback that says instrument-failure rather than `Drift:`. Decide first whether a self-test failure SHOULD file an issue at all — arguably yes, since a steward whose instrument breaks silently is the exact failure mode this lane exists to prevent.

verifyBy.method: re-run the Open-finding body under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` with finding.txt absent and confirm it reaches the issue-create call with a non-misleading title

items.title: Alarm labelled a transient network failure 'Drift:' and omitted the reason entirely (production issue #2)
items.note: CAUGHT IN PRODUCTION 2026-07-25, not by review. CI run 30168372746 (push of 59cd3a1, 17:48Z) failed and auto-filed issue #2 titled 'Drift: bounds-ledger re-verification (2026-07-25)' over a body reading '223 claim(s): 222 hold, 0 broken/unreachable' — self-contradictory. No record drifted: reverify.mjs --check hit a transient network error, printed 'error: fetch failed', exited 2; the claims step then ran via if:'!cancelled()' and everything held; the next push ten minutes later was green. TWO DEFECTS. (1) A tool error was titled 'Drift:', asserting a mathematical record moved when none did — the title extraction found no CHANGED/ADDED/REMOVED and no BROKEN/UNREACHABLE lines and fell through to the generic default, which is still prefixed 'Drift:'. (2) The reason was invisible: reverify.mjs reports errors via console.error (stderr) but the step piped only stdout (`| tee`), so 'error: fetch failed' reached the CI log and never the issue body. Same failure family as the 2026-07-24 never-armed defect from the opposite direction — that alarm could not speak, this one spoke and said the wrong thing. Cost model: a false 'Drift:' burns a reader's time hunting a record change that never happened, and repeated flakes train us to skim past Drift: issues, which is how a REAL drift gets missed. Finding: docs/findings/2026-07-25-alarm-called-a-network-flake-a-drift.md.
items.closeWhen: A tool/network error produces an honestly-titled issue that states the cause, and a real drift still titles as a drift.
items.resolution: FIXED 2026-07-25 same day. (a) `2>&1` added to both piped check steps so stderr lands in finding.txt and therefore in the issue body; (b) the title now branches three ways instead of falling through — 'Drift: <what moved>' on real drift/claim lines, 'Check error: … could not complete' when finding.txt contains an ^error: line, 'Re-verification failed' otherwise (A-4 supplies a fourth, 'Instrument failure', when finding.txt does not exist at all). VERIFIED BY EXECUTION under GitHub's exact shell (bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail) against four real inputs including a byte-accurate replay of run 30168372746: replay => 'Check error: bounds-ledger re-verification could not complete (2026-07-25)'; absent finding.txt => 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (2026-07-25)'; injected mirror drift => 'Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)'; broken pin => 'Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)'. npm test green; all 5 piped workflow steps still carry shell: bash.
items.note2: RESOLVES TWO SWEEP UNKNOWNS, for free and within the hour. The 2026-07-25 gate-execution sweep marked the composite CI failure path (if: failure() -> gh issue create) and if:'!cancelled()' on the claims step as UNKNOWN, because closing them would have required pushing a corrupted mirror. Production answered both: the issue-filing path FIRES (issue #2 exists) and !cancelled() FIRES (claim output appears in the body although the mirror step had already failed) — and the output was WRONG, which a green could never have revealed. Method lesson worth keeping: the honest UNKNOWN left the question open, so the evidence was recognised when it arrived; a fabricated green would have closed it and issue #2 would have been read as a real drift.
items.note3: DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: retry/backoff on a transient fetch failure. One flake in four days does not justify it, and suppressing the alarm is the wrong direction. If check-error issues become frequent, add retry inside reverify.mjs — never silence the step.

verifyBy.method: replay the deployed Open-finding body under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` against a finding.txt containing an ^error: line and confirm the title says Check error, not Drift

items.title: OPPORTUNITY: adopt erdosproblems.com as the second stewarded surface — and route corrections as PRs to teorth/erdosproblems instead of email
items.note: Filed 2026-07-25. VERIFIED FACTS: (a) github.com/teorth/erdosproblems is PUBLIC and actively maintained (pushed 2026-07-25T17:27Z, ~16.7MB), described as the community database behind erdosproblems.com — reachable from anywhere via api.github.com/raw, so it is NOT affected by the site's datacenter-IP block; (b) it ships data/problems.yaml (396KB, 19742 lines), schema/, scripts/ and a 21KB CONTRIBUTING.md, i.e. it ACCEPTS CONTRIBUTIONS; (c) problems.yaml carries METADATA only (number, prize, status, oeis, formalized, tags) — the numeric bounds live in the site page prose/LaTeX. CORRECTION vs this item's first draft: I initially wrote that the whole site is machine-readable. It is not, from CI — erdosproblems.com 403s datacenter IPs (see W-3 note2). The GITHUB REPO is machine-readable from anywhere; the SITE is only readable from a residential IP. Any design here must be built on the repo, not on scraping the site from CI.
items.note2: WHY THIS MATTERS FOR G-1, which is the real point. G-1 needs at least one EXTERNALLY-ACKNOWLEDGED correction and that metric is currently 0, resting entirely on one email to one busy maintainer who owes us nothing. Two independent improvements are now available: (1) SCALE THE CATCHES — erdosproblems.com is the most-used index in the field and we already know it goes stale (that is the lane founding finding). Systematically diffing its bounds against Tao curated table across many problems turns one lucky catch into a repeatable pipeline of correction candidates. (2) CHANGE THE CHANNEL — a PR against a community database with a CONTRIBUTING.md is mechanically reviewable and leaves a public, dated, attributable record. An accepted PR IS an external acknowledgement, and unlike an email it cannot be silently ignored into ambiguity. Email put the north-star metric behind an inbox; a PR puts it behind a merge button.
items.note3: SEQUENCING / CAUTION. Real feature build, not cleanup — do not start it inside a close-out. Order: (i) read CONTRIBUTING.md properly, since contribution norms are the whole point of choosing this channel; (ii) settle whether bound corrections are even in scope for that repo, given problems.yaml is metadata-only — IF THE SITE PROSE IS NOT COMMUNITY-EDITABLE THEN THE PR CHANNEL DOES NOT APPLY TO BOUND CORRECTIONS and only the scale half survives; this is the most likely way the whole item is wrong, so check it FIRST; (iii) build any mirror on the GitHub repo (reachable from CI), never on scraping the site from CI (403); (iv) outward contact — and a PR is outward contact — stays behind the adversarial refute-it review AND David's outward-send gate, unchanged; (v) prefer extending the existing mirror+claims machinery over new scripts.
items.note4: PHASE-0 SCOPING VERDICT 2026-07-25 (second session, David asked in-pane; read-only, no contact). THE HINGE FAILS FOR BOUNDS: the repo contains NO problem prose and NO numeric bounds. Evidence, direct not summarized: GitHub code search for 0.380876/0.379005 = 0 hits (weak alone — files >350KB unindexed), so README.md (421KB, the generated table) and data/problems.yaml (396KB) were fetched raw and grepped locally for 0.380876/0.379005/0.380868 — all three ABSENT from both; repo tree has no per-problem content (docs/ is the JS table viewer, data/ is problems.yaml + statistics). CONTRIBUTING.md scope: edits to the metadata table ('particularly with regards to the OEIS column'); for mathematical context it directs contributors to 'the corresponding problem page on the erdosproblems.com site' — i.e. the site's per-problem comment/forum pages are the sanctioned public venue for problem-content discussion. Database credited 'Maintained by Thomas Bloom and Terence Tao.' CONSEQUENCES: (1) bound corrections can NEVER be PRs to this repo — that half of the original design is dead as imagined; (2) the PR channel SURVIVES for the metadata table (status/OEIS/tags) — an accepted metadata-correction PR is still a public dated external ack, so adopting problems.yaml as the second stewarded surface keeps the channel alive with a different catch type (status staleness instead of bound staleness); (3) for the /36 BOUND correction specifically, the sanctioned public channel is a comment on erdosproblems.com/36 — outward contact, adversarial review + David gate, candidate fallback if the W-3 email stays unanswered at the ~2026-08-24 decision point.
items.closeWhen: Either erdosproblems.com is adopted as a second stewarded surface with claims under CI, or a deliberate decision is recorded that it should not be (with the reason).

verifyBy.method: the second surface re-verifies in CI alongside the first, or a decision doc explains why not

items.title: Watch for acknowledgement of the erdosproblems.com/36 correction — the first external ack, which is G-1's close condition
items.note: A-3's correction was emailed to the erdosproblems.com maintainer 2026-07-24 (David sent it). SENDING IS NOT ACKNOWLEDGEMENT — the lane's north-star metric (externally-acknowledged corrections/confirmations) remains 0 until one of: (a) a reply from the maintainer, (b) erdosproblems.com/36 updates its upper bound to 0.380868, or (c) the page's 'last edited' date moves. TWO WATCH LEGS, and both need David: the site 403s automated fetch (so claim C-7 stays manual: true and reports UNVERIFIED by design — a bot fetch proves nothing), and the reply lands in David's inbox, not ours. Ask: David pastes/forwards any reply, and re-checks the page by hand periodically. Do NOT substitute an agent fetch for either leg. If the page updates, C-7's expected value flips from 0.380876 to 0.380868 and ledger/claims.json needs the pin updated deliberately.
items.closeWhen: An acknowledgement is recorded — a maintainer reply, or a hand-verified page update to 0.380868 — OR a deliberate decision that no response is coming and the watch ends.
items.onTrigger: When David supplies evidence (pasted/forwarded reply, or a hand-browse showing the page changed): (1) file the ack as a finding in docs/findings/ quoting the evidence verbatim with date; (2) if the page now shows 0.380868, flip C-7 in ledger/claims.json — expect 0.380876 -> 0.380868, statement rewritten, lastHandVerify updated (deliberate hand edit; C-7 is a hand claim, NOT generated); (3) update G-1 note3 — external-ack metric 0 -> 1, its second close condition met; (4) close W-3 with closedAt + the evidence pointer; (5) post a bus task-complete (this is the lane's north-star event). If instead David decides no response is coming, close W-3 recording that decision — do NOT silently let it age out.

verifyBy.method: A maintainer reply supplied by David, OR a hand/local re-verification of erdosproblems.com/36 showing the bound or last-edited date changed. A CI fetch does NOT count — runners are 403ed. A local `npm run check` DOES count.
verifyBy.owner: david (reply leg) + any local session (page leg)

items.note2: PAGE-LEG AUTOMATION ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED 2026-07-25 — the 403 is REAL but IP-DEPENDENT. David hand-checked the page (unchanged, still 0.380876 / last edited 23 Jan 2026) and asked for a Playwright poller. Testing the premise first showed a plain Node fetch from a residential IP returns HTTP 200 with the bound readable, so C-7 was automated and a C-8 added. CI went red four minutes later: from a GitHub Actions runner the same URL returns HTTP 403 (UNREACHABLE C-7, C-8). Datacenter-IP block. REVERTED: C-7 is manual: true again, C-8 removed, ledger back to 223 claims / 222 hold / 1 UNVERIFIED. Finding: docs/findings/2026-07-25-the-403-that-wasnt.md.
items.note3: WHAT THIS WATCH ACTUALLY NEEDS, corrected. (1) A maintainer REPLY — lands in David's inbox, only he can supply it. Forward or paste. (2) The PAGE state — CI cannot check it (403 from runners), but an agent running `npm run check` ON A RESIDENTIAL CONNECTION re-verifies C-7 mechanically. That is the durable upgrade from this episode: the page-check is no longer a screenshot round-trip, it is a local command any session can run.
